details: @randev404/baileys@2.1.1 is a modified fork of the WhatsApp library @whiskeysockets/baileys published under an unofficial scope, and it performs unsolicited actions on the WhatsApp account of whoever installs it. On every makeWASocket() call src/Socket/index.js prints a promotional banner and registers a connection.update handler; as soon as the WhatsApp connection opens it calls autoFollowChannels(sock) from src/custom.js, which subscribes the victim's account to five hard-coded channels (120363424153860594@newsletter, 120363404374842519@newsletter, 120363429448999317@newsletter, 120363422841048901@newsletter, 120363410493464535@newsletter) via sock.newsletterFollow(), two seconds apart, with no user consent or configuration. The behaviour is on by default (autoFollow: true) and is not part of upstream Baileys. The package also replaces upstream crypto/hash helpers with a third-party bridge dependency (@rexxhayanasi/wangcap-id-bridge: hkdf, expandAppStateKeys, LTHashAntiTampering) and pulls an optional @rexxhayanasi/elaina-anchorguard module via dynamic import. No network endpoint beyond WhatsApp's own hosts and no install hooks are involved; the abuse channel is the authenticated WhatsApp session itself. @randev404/baileys is a squat fork of the widely used @whiskeysockets/baileys WhatsApp library (basename "baileys", published under an unrelated scope, with a hardcoded pairing code "RANDEV12"). src/custom.js holds five hardcoded WhatsApp newsletter ids (120363424153860594@newsletter, 120363404374842519@newsletter, 120363429448999317@newsletter, 120363422841048901@newsletter, 120363410493464535@newsletter) with autoFollow: true, and src/Socket/index.js calls showBanner() at socket creation and autoFollowChannels(sock) whenever the connection reports open. Once a developer pairs their own WhatsApp account through this library, the library therefore forces that account to follow the five attacker-chosen channels, silently and with no way to opt out other than editing the package, inflating the channels' subscriber counts at the expense of the installer's account identity. The same createWASocket path also lazily pulls the author's secondary packages @rexxhayanasi/elaina-anchorguard and @rexxhayanasi/wangcap-id-bridge at runtime.
